programme.title: North by Northwest
programme.desc: Roger O Thornhill is an advertising executive mistaken for a government agent by a group of foreign spies led by James Vandamm. Initially bemused, when he is accused of murdering a UN official he is forced to go on the run. He survives murderous attacks in both auction rooms and deserted cornfields of the Midwest, leading to one of cinema's most memorable climaxes on Mount Rushmore.

programme.title: Winterwatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham introduces a classic documentary from the BBC's archive, which takes a look at the worst winter of the 20th century in 1963. He also explores what we now know about how this big freeze affected Britain's wildlife, and how it would cope if we experienced another equally bad winter.

programme.title: Hitchcock at the NFT
programme.desc: In his 70th year, Alfred Hitchcock came to the National Film Theatre in London to talk to fellow director Bryan Forbes and to answer questions from an audience of film enthusiasts.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: A look at the life of acting legend Michael Caine, using rarely seen television interviews and classic archive clips to tell the story of one Britain's most successful actors.

programme.title: Thailand: Earth's Tropical Paradise
programme.desc: Southern Thailand is the Thailand people think they know. It is a place of both spectacular natural beauty and of wild parties, but behind this well-known image is also a place of unexpected surprise, where spirituality pervades every bit of life. For the animals that live here, this is natural wonderland.

programme.title: City Beneath the Waves: Pavlopetri
programme.desc: Off the southern coast of mainland Greece lies the oldest submerged city in the world, Pavlopetri. Led by underwater archaeologist Dr Jon Henderson, an international team of experts attempt to prise age-old secrets from the complex of streets and stone buildings laying less than five metres below the surface. State-of-the-art CGI helps to raise the city from the seabed for the first time in 3500 years.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Robert Robinson hosts the game of word definitions and deceptions. Joining team captains Frank Muir and Patrick Campbell are Patrick Mower, Russell Harty, Nanette Newman and Gabrielle Drake.

programme.title: Face the Music
programme.desc: Joseph Cooper invites viewers to match their musical wits against Joyce Grenfell, David Attenborough and Richard Baker. With guest musician Sir Keith Faulkner.

programme.sub-title: Frank Gehry: The Architect Says `Why Can't I?'
programme.desc: A fascinating look at the career of architect Frank Gehry, who despite being well into his eighties remains one of the world's most celebrated and famously provocative creative forces.

programme.desc: A profile of architect Frank Gehry, acclaimed worldwide for his audacious and distinctive buildings. First broadcast in 1993.
